routines.title: Neck & Shoulder Reset
routines.subtitle: Ease the tightness screens leave in your neck.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Move your head slowly for the first minute. Drink some water, and try putting your screen at eye height for the rest of the day.

routines.title: Foot Relief
routines.subtitle: Ease tired arches after a long day standing.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Do the other foot even if it does not hurt — feet like to match. Drink some water. If your heel is angry in the morning, roll a frozen water bottle under it for five minutes.

routines.title: Hand & Wrist Reset
routines.subtitle: Undo a day of typing and scrolling.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Shake your hands out and let them rest. If your fingers go numb or tingly while you work, stand up and move every half hour.

routines.title: Scalp & Sleep
routines.subtitle: An Indian head massage you do lying in bed.
needs: A towel over the pillow if you use oil
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: There is nothing to do at the end. Leave your arms where they land, keep your eyes closed, and let sleep come on its own.

routines.title: Face Lymphatic Glow
routines.subtitle: Feather-light strokes for a puffy morning face.
needs: A drop of facial oil optional
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Drink a glass of water and sit tall for a few minutes. Doing this lightly most mornings does far more than doing it hard once.

routines.title: Jaw & TMJ Release
routines.subtitle: Unclench the jaw you grind all night.
routines.reviewedBy: Reviewed by a licensed massage therapist
routines.aftercare: Keep your lips together and your teeth apart for the rest of the day. Soft food tonight if your jaw feels tired, and a warm flannel on the cheek helps.

steps.title: Roll your shoulders and breathe
steps.body: Sit tall and roll both shoulders slowly backward. Let them drop a little lower with every breath out.
steps.sensationCue: Loose, easy movement. No pinching at the top of the circle.
steps.rhythm: One slow roll every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as your shoulders drop
steps.voiceScript: Sit tall with your feet flat on the floor. Roll both shoulders slowly backward, and let them settle a little lower each time you breathe out. There is no rush at all here.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rush the roll. Slow circles loosen more than fast ones.

steps.title: Warm the side of your neck
steps.body: Rest your right palm on the left side of your neck. Stroke slowly down to the shoulder, then swap hands and sides.
steps.sensationCue: Warm and smooth. Nothing sharp or scratchy.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath in, slower breath out
steps.voiceScript: Rest your right palm flat against the left side of your neck. Stroke slowly down towards the shoulder, lift off, and start again from the top. After about twenty seconds, swap hands and do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press hard yet. This step only warms the skin and muscle.
steps.caution: Stay on the soft side of the neck. Never press the front of your throat.

steps.title: Squeeze the top of your shoulder
steps.body: Reach across and grip the ridge of muscle on top of the opposite shoulder. Squeeze, lift it slightly, and let go.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache that softens as you work. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one squeeze per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Reach your right hand across to your left shoulder and take that ridge of muscle between your thumb and fingers. Squeeze, lift it a little, then let it go, like kneading dough. Give each side about thirty seconds.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pinch with your fingertips. Use the whole flat of your fingers.

steps.title: Hold the tightest spot
steps.body: Feel along the top of your shoulder for the sorest lump. Press straight down and hold still for thirty seconds each side.
steps.sensationCue: A strong ache that fades by about half while you hold.
steps.rhythm: Still — hold, do not rub
steps.breathCue: Breathe out into the pressure
steps.voiceScript: Feel along the top of your shoulder until you find the sorest little lump. Press straight down into it with your fingertips and simply hold, counting thirty slow seconds. Then ease off and do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rub the spot. Still, steady pressure is what lets it let go.
steps.caution: If the ache turns sharp, burning or shoots down your arm, come off it.

steps.title: Work the base of your skull
steps.body: Curl your fingertips up under the bony ridge at the back of your head. Make small, slow circles either side of the middle.
steps.sensationCue: A melting release that spreads up into your head. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Three or four circles, then move a thumb-width
steps.breathCue: Let your head get heavy on your fingers
steps.voiceScript: Curl your fingertips up under the bony ridge at the back of your head, where the skull meets the neck. Make small, slow circles, and let the weight of your head rest into your fingers. Work outward towards your ears a thumb-width at a time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not dig with your nails. Use the soft pads of your fingers.
steps.caution: Stay either side of the bony bumps of the spine, never on them.

steps.title: Roll a ball against the wall
steps.body: Stand with a tennis ball between the wall and the muscle beside your spine. Lean in and roll slowly, pausing where it complains.
steps.sensationCue: Firm pressure you control by how much you lean in. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Pause ten seconds on any sore spot
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you lean in
steps.voiceScript: Stand with your back to a wall and trap a tennis ball between the wall and the muscle beside your spine. Bend your knees to roll slowly up and down, and stop for ten seconds on anything that complains. Swap to the other side halfway through.
steps.commonMistake: Do not roll fast. Slow beats hard every single time.
steps.caution: Keep the ball off your spine. Stay on the muscle either side of it.

steps.title: Lengthen the side of your neck
steps.body: Drop your left ear towards your left shoulder and rest your left hand on your head. Let its weight hold you there twenty seconds, then swap.
steps.sensationCue: A long, comfortable pull down the side. Never a pinch.
steps.rhythm: Hold twenty seconds each side
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let the shoulder sink
steps.voiceScript: Drop your left ear towards your left shoulder and lay your left hand gently over your head. Use only the weight of the hand, never a pull, and hold for about twenty seconds. Come up slowly, then do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not lift the opposite shoulder. Let it stay down and heavy.
steps.caution: Never force the stretch. Weight of the hand only, and stop if anything tingles.

steps.title: Rake your fingertips down
steps.body: Draw your fingertips slowly from the base of your skull down your neck and out over the shoulder. Get lighter with every pass.
steps.sensationCue: Shivery and calming, like the work is closing.
steps.rhythm: One slow rake every four seconds, hands alternating
steps.breathCue: Long, easy breaths
steps.voiceScript: Draw your fingertips slowly from the base of your skull, down the neck and out across the shoulder. Alternate hands, and make each pass a little lighter than the one before.

steps.title: Rest your hands and finish
steps.body: Rest both palms on the tops of your shoulders. Take three slow breaths, then let your hands slide away.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth and stillness. Shoulders sitting lower than before.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Three long breaths out
steps.voiceScript: Cross your hands over and rest a palm on each shoulder. Do not move at all. Take three slow breaths, then let your hands slide down into your lap.
steps.commonMistake: Do not jump straight back to your desk. Give it one quiet moment.

steps.title: Warm the whole foot
steps.body: Cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Sandwich the foot between both palms and stroke firmly from toes to ankle, over and over.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth and blood coming back into a cold foot.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out with each stroke
steps.voiceScript: Sit down and cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Sandwich your foot between both palms and stroke firmly from the toes up to the ankle, again and again, until the whole foot feels warm.
steps.commonMistake: Do not rush to the sore spot. Warm the whole foot first.

steps.title: Loosen the ankle
steps.body: Hold your heel still with one hand. With the other, circle the foot slowly five times each way.
steps.sensationCue: Easy movement. No clicking, grinding or pinching.
steps.rhythm: One slow circle every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Keep breathing — do not hold it
steps.voiceScript: Hold your heel still in one hand so the ankle cannot cheat. With the other hand, take the front of the foot and circle it slowly, five times one way and five times back.
steps.commonMistake: Do not swing the whole leg. Only the foot should move.

steps.title: Thumb-walk the arch
steps.body: Press your thumb into the heel and walk it forward along the arch in small bites, like a caterpillar. Make three passes.
steps.sensationCue: Tender spots that ease after a few seconds of pressure.
steps.rhythm: About one small bite per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on the tender spots
steps.voiceScript: Press your thumb into the middle of the heel, then bend and straighten it to walk forward along the arch in tiny bites, like a caterpillar. Take three slow passes from heel to the ball of the foot, and pause a few seconds anywhere tender.
steps.commonMistake: Do not slide. Press, ease off, move a little — that is the walk.

steps.title: Stretch the sole open
steps.body: Put both thumbs in the centre of the sole. Draw them slowly apart to open the foot outward, then start again lower down.
steps.sensationCue: The sole broadening. A slow, spreading stretch.
steps.rhythm: One slow spread every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you spread
steps.voiceScript: Place both thumbs together in the centre of the sole, with your fingers wrapped over the top of the foot. Draw the thumbs slowly apart so the sole opens outward. Move a little further down and do it again.
steps.commonMistake: Do not go fast. This kind of tissue only gives to slow, patient pressure.

steps.title: Work the heel
steps.body: Make firm circles into the fleshy pad of the heel with your knuckles. Keep the circles small and slow.
steps.sensationCue: Deep, dull and satisfying. Never sharp or burning.
steps.rhythm: About one small circle per second
steps.breathCue: Long breath out as you press in
steps.voiceScript: Make a loose fist and press your knuckles into the fleshy pad of the heel. Work in small, firm circles, covering the whole heel. Keep it slow, and let it be a deep, dull feeling rather than a sharp one.
steps.commonMistake: Do not hammer at it. Sink in slowly and let the pressure build.
steps.caution: Ease right off if you feel a sharp, stabbing pain under the heel.

steps.title: Slide between the foot bones
steps.body: Turn to the top of the foot. Slide your thumb along each groove between the long bones, from the toes back towards the ankle.
steps.sensationCue: Narrow lines of tenderness that ease as you pass.
steps.rhythm: One slow slide per groove
steps.breathCue: Keep your breathing steady
steps.voiceScript: Turn your attention to the top of the foot. Find the grooves between the long bones and slide your thumb along each one, from the base of the toes back towards the ankle. Four grooves, one slow pass each.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press on the bones themselves. Stay in the soft grooves.

steps.title: Pull and circle each toe
steps.body: Take each toe in turn. Pull gently for two seconds, then circle it once each way.
steps.sensationCue: A tiny release in each joint. Never a crack or a wrench.
steps.rhythm: About six seconds per toe
steps.breathCue: Easy breaths, no holding
steps.voiceScript: Take hold of your big toe between your thumb and finger. Pull gently for a couple of seconds, then circle it once each way. Work along all five toes, then give the whole foot a little shake.
steps.commonMistake: Do not yank for a click. A gentle, steady pull is enough.

steps.title: Roll it out with a ball
steps.body: Stand and roll a tennis ball under your foot, from heel to toes. Pause ten seconds on any spot that complains.
steps.sensationCue: Firm pressure you control by how much weight you lean in.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you lean your weight in
steps.voiceScript: Stand up and put a tennis ball under the arch of your foot. Roll it slowly from heel to toes, and choose your own pressure by how much weight you let down onto it. When something complains, stop and rest on it for ten seconds.
steps.commonMistake: Do not race the ball back and forth. Slow rolling does the work.
steps.caution: Hold a wall or chair for balance. Keep your weight light if the skin is tender.

steps.title: Stretch the calf
steps.body: Put both palms on a wall and step this foot back. Keep the heel down and lean in for thirty seconds.
steps.sensationCue: A long pull through the back of the calf. Never a sharp grab.
steps.rhythm: Hold thirty seconds, then ease out slowly
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and sink into it
steps.voiceScript: Stand facing a wall and press both palms into it. Step the foot you have been working back behind you, keep that heel flat on the floor, and lean your hips towards the wall. Hold for thirty slow seconds, then come out of it gently.
steps.commonMistake: Do not let the back heel lift. That is where the stretch lives.

steps.title: Finish with long strokes
steps.body: Stroke the whole foot from toes to ankle, getting lighter each time. Then swap feet and work the other side the same way.
steps.sensationCue: Light, warm and finished.
steps.rhythm: One feather-light stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow, quiet breaths
steps.voiceScript: Sandwich the foot between your palms one last time and stroke from the toes up to the ankle, getting lighter with every pass. Rest it on the floor and notice how different the two feet feel. Then start again on the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not skip the second foot. Feet like to match.

steps.title: Warm your hands
steps.body: Rub your palms together until they feel warm. Then stroke firmly from the fingers of one hand up over the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth spreading through cold, stiff fingers.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out as you stroke
steps.voiceScript: Rub your palms together briskly until they feel warm. Then wrap one hand around the other and stroke firmly from the fingers up over the wrist, a few times each side.

steps.title: Circle your wrists slowly
steps.body: Let your hands hang loose and circle both wrists five times each way. Keep the circles slow and easy.
steps.sensationCue: Smooth, quiet movement. No clicks or catching.
steps.rhythm: One circle every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out through the slow part
steps.voiceScript: Let your hands hang loose from the wrists. Circle them slowly five times one way, then five times back, and keep your fingers soft the whole time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not force a big circle. Go as far as feels easy, no further.

steps.title: Press your palm open
steps.body: Put both thumbs in the middle of your palm. Draw them slowly apart to open the hand, then start again a little lower.
steps.sensationCue: A broad, spreading stretch across the palm.
steps.rhythm: One slow spread every five seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you spread
steps.voiceScript: Turn one palm up and place both thumbs together in the middle of it, fingers wrapped around the back. Draw your thumbs slowly apart so the palm opens out. Work up and down the hand, then swap.
steps.commonMistake: Do not dig into one point. Spread wide and slow instead.

steps.title: Work the base of your thumb
steps.body: Find the fleshy mound at the base of your thumb. Make small, slow circles into it with your other thumb.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache right where the mouse sits. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one small circle per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out into the sore spots
steps.voiceScript: Find the fleshy mound at the base of your thumb, the part that does all the gripping and scrolling. Press your other thumb into it and make small, slow circles over the whole mound. Give it about twenty seconds each hand.
steps.commonMistake: Do not squeeze the whole hand. Aim for that one fleshy mound.
steps.caution: Ease off if you get pins and needles in your fingers.

steps.title: Slide between the hand bones
steps.body: Turn your hand palm down. Slide your thumb along each groove between the long bones, from the knuckles back to the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Narrow lines of tenderness that ease as you pass.
steps.rhythm: One slow slide per groove
steps.breathCue: Steady, unhurried breathing
steps.voiceScript: Turn one hand palm down and feel the grooves between the long bones on the back of it. Slide your other thumb slowly along each groove, from the knuckle back towards the wrist. Four grooves on each hand.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press on the bones. Stay in the soft grooves between them.

steps.title: Squeeze your forearm
steps.body: Wrap your hand around the meat of the opposite forearm, just below the elbow. Squeeze and release your way down to the wrist.
steps.sensationCue: Tight ropes of muscle softening under the squeeze.
steps.rhythm: One squeeze per second, moving as you go
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you squeeze
steps.voiceScript: Wrap your hand around the fleshy top of the opposite forearm, just below the elbow. Squeeze, let go, and work your way down to the wrist. Do the top of the forearm and the underside, then swap arms.
steps.commonMistake: Do not skip this. Most typing ache starts in the forearm, not the hand.

steps.title: Pull and circle each finger
steps.body: Take each finger in turn. Pull gently for two seconds, then circle it once each way.
steps.sensationCue: A small release in every knuckle. Never a wrench.
steps.rhythm: About three seconds per finger
steps.breathCue: Easy breaths, shoulders down
steps.voiceScript: Take each finger between your thumb and finger, one at a time. Pull gently for a couple of seconds, then circle it once each way. Work through all five, then swap hands.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pull for a crack. A steady, gentle pull is plenty.

steps.title: Stretch and shake out
steps.body: Press your palms together in front of your chest and lower them until you feel a stretch. Hold, then shake your hands out loose.
steps.sensationCue: A gentle pull through the wrist. Nothing pinching in front.
steps.rhythm: Hold fifteen seconds, then shake for ten
steps.breathCue: Long breath out while you hold
steps.voiceScript: Press your palms together in front of your chest, fingers pointing up. Lower your hands slowly until you feel a gentle pull through the wrists, and hold there for fifteen seconds. Then let go and shake your hands out loose.
steps.caution: Stop the stretch if it pinches in the front of the wrist.

steps.title: Rest your palms and settle
steps.body: Lie on your back and rest both palms on your forehead. Take three slow breaths and let your head get heavy in the pillow.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth on the forehead. The pillow taking your weight.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Long, slow breath out through your nose
steps.voiceScript: Lie on your back with a pillow under your head and rest both palms across your forehead. Do not move at all. Take three slow breaths and let your head get heavier in the pillow with each one.
steps.commonMistake: Do not start rubbing straight away. The stillness sets everything up.

steps.title: Smooth your forehead
steps.body: Draw your fingertips from the middle of your brow out to the temples. Lift off, start a little higher, and work up to the hairline.
steps.sensationCue: The frown letting go. Smooth and unhurried.
steps.rhythm: One slow sweep every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out along each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Bring your fingertips to the middle of your brow, just above your nose. Draw them out towards your temples, lift off, and start again a little higher. Keep going until you have covered the whole forehead up to the hairline.

steps.title: Circle along your hairline
steps.body: Set your fingertips at your hairline and make small circles. Move the skin over the bone rather than sliding across it.
steps.sensationCue: The scalp shifting in one piece. No scratching.
steps.rhythm: Three or four circles, then move a finger-width
steps.breathCue: Quiet, even breathing
steps.voiceScript: Put your fingertips along your hairline and make small circles there. The trick is to move the skin over the bone rather than sliding your fingers across the skin. Work slowly from the middle out towards each temple.
steps.commonMistake: Do not scratch with your nails. Move the skin, not your fingers.

steps.title: Shampoo circles all over
steps.body: Spread your fingers and work all over your scalp, like washing your hair without water. Cover the top, the sides and the back.
steps.sensationCue: A tingling, loosening feeling spreading over your head.
steps.rhythm: Slow circles, moving on every few seconds
steps.breathCue: Keep your breathing long and quiet
steps.voiceScript: Spread your fingers and work them all over your scalp, like you are washing your hair without any water. Take your time over the sides above your ears, then the top, then as much of the back as you can reach against the pillow.
steps.commonMistake: Do not only work the top. The sides above your ears hold the most.

steps.title: Lift and release your hair
steps.body: Take a small handful of hair close to the roots. Lift until you feel a gentle pull, hold two seconds, then let go.
steps.sensationCue: A pleasant tug at the roots. Never enough to sting.
steps.rhythm: Lift, hold two seconds, release, move on
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you let go
steps.voiceScript: Gather a small handful of hair close to the roots. Lift it straight up until you feel a gentle pull across the scalp, hold for two seconds, and let it go. Move around your head a handful at a time.
steps.commonMistake: Do not grab the ends. Hold close to the scalp so nothing tugs.
steps.caution: Skip this one if your hair is fine, fragile or thinning.

steps.title: Press under your skull
steps.body: Slide your fingertips under the bony ridge at the back of your head. Let the weight of your head press into them and hold.
steps.sensationCue: A slow melt that spreads up into your head.
steps.rhythm: Hold twenty seconds, then move a thumb-width outward
steps.breathCue: Long breath out as you sink in
steps.voiceScript: Slide your fingertips under the bony ridge at the back of your head, either side of the middle. Now stop pushing and simply let the weight of your head rest down onto them. Hold for twenty seconds, then move your fingers out a little towards your ears.
steps.commonMistake: Do not lift your head to help. Let the pillow and your hands do it.
steps.caution: Stay either side of the bony spine, never on it.

steps.title: Circle your temples slowly
steps.body: Put two fingers on each temple, just above the ear. Make circles so slow you could count each one.
steps.sensationCue: Pressure easing behind the eyes. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One circle every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Slower out than in
steps.voiceScript: Rest two fingers on each temple, just above and in front of the ear. Circle them so slowly that you could count each turn. Let your elbows be heavy and your jaw soft while you do it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press hard here. The temple is thin and likes light work.

steps.title: Cup your palms over your eyes
steps.body: Cup both palms over your closed eyes so no weight lands on them. Rest in that darkness for a slow count of thirty.
steps.sensationCue: Warm darkness. No weight at all on the eyes.
steps.rhythm: Still
steps.breathCue: Breathe out longer than you breathe in
steps.voiceScript: Close your eyes and cup both palms over them, so the edges of your hands rest on the bone and nothing touches the eyes themselves. Stay in that warm darkness for a slow count of thirty, and let your breathing get longer.
steps.caution: Rest your hands on the bone around the eyes. Never press on the eyeball.

steps.title: Let your hands drift down
steps.body: Let your arms slide down onto the bed and stop moving. Stay still and let your breathing get slower and slower.
steps.sensationCue: Heaviness, quiet, nothing left to do.
steps.rhythm: No movement at all
steps.breathCue: Slow, quiet breaths — let them fade
steps.voiceScript: Let your arms slide down onto the bed and leave them wherever they land. There is nothing left to do now. Let your breathing get slower, and let yourself drift off whenever you are ready.
steps.commonMistake: Do not do one more bit. Stopping is the last step.

steps.title: Open the hollows above your collarbone
steps.body: Rest your fingertips in the soft hollows just above your collarbones. Press in feather-light and release, like a slow pump, twenty times.
steps.sensationCue: Barely-there pressure. Skin moves, muscle does not.
steps.rhythm: One gentle pump every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out on each press
steps.voiceScript: Cross your hands and rest your fingertips in the soft hollows just above your collarbones. Press in as lightly as if you were pressing on a soap bubble, then release. Twenty slow pumps, and no more pressure than that.
steps.commonMistake: Do not push deep. This work sits just under the skin.
steps.caution: Feather-light only, and stay well off the front of your throat.

steps.title: Sweep down your neck
steps.body: Lay flat fingers just below your ears. Stroke slowly down the sides of your neck to your collarbones, ten times each side.
steps.sensationCue: A light drag on the skin. Nothing pressing inward.
steps.rhythm: One slow sweep every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Long breath out down each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Lay flat fingers on the sides of your neck, just below your ears. Stroke slowly downward to the collarbones, so lightly that the skin barely moves ahead of your hand. Ten passes each side, and always downward.
steps.commonMistake: Do not work upward. Everything drains downward from here.
steps.caution: Keep to the soft sides of the neck. Never press the front of your throat.

steps.title: Pump in front of your ears
steps.body: Place two fingers in the small dip just in front of each ear. Press in lightly and release, twenty slow pumps.
steps.sensationCue: A soft, hollow feeling. No dragging on the skin.
steps.rhythm: One pump every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Quiet, even breathing
steps.voiceScript: Find the small dip just in front of each ear, level with your cheekbone. Rest two fingers there and press in very lightly, then release, twenty times. This is the doorway everything else will be swept towards.

steps.title: Drain your jawline to your ears
steps.body: Set flat fingers either side of your chin. Glide them along your jawline out to your ears, then lift off and start again.
steps.sensationCue: A light, gliding sweep. Never a drag or a pull.
steps.rhythm: One glide every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out with each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Set flat fingers either side of your chin, one hand for each side of the jaw. Glide them along the jawline out towards your ears, finishing in that dip you just pumped. Lift off, go back to the chin, and repeat about ten times.
steps.commonMistake: Do not stop halfway. Always finish the sweep at the ear.

steps.title: Sweep your cheeks toward your ears
steps.body: Lay flat fingers beside your nose. Sweep out across your cheeks to your ears, so light that the skin barely moves ahead of you.
steps.sensationCue: Almost nothing — a whisper of movement. Never a rub.
steps.rhythm: One sweep every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out along each sweep
steps.voiceScript: Lay flat fingers on your cheeks, either side of your nose. Sweep them outward towards your ears, keeping the touch so light it is almost nothing. Work the upper cheek, then the middle, then along the top of the jaw.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press into the cheek. Light and wide beats deep and small.

steps.title: Trace under your eyes
steps.body: Use your ring finger to trace the bone under each eye, from the inner corner out to the temple. Repeat ten times.
steps.sensationCue: Feather-light along the bone. No pull on the eyelid.
steps.rhythm: One slow trace every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Soft, quiet breaths
steps.voiceScript: Use your ring finger, because it presses the least. Trace the bone under each eye, starting at the inner corner and travelling out to the temple, then carry on down in front of the ear. Ten light passes.
steps.commonMistake: Do not stretch the skin. The skin here is the thinnest on your body.
steps.caution: Stay on the bony rim under the eye. Never press on the eyeball itself.

steps.title: Smooth your brows outward
steps.body: Run your thumbs along the ridge under your eyebrows, from the inner ends out to the temples. Finish each pass at the hairline.
steps.sensationCue: A pleasant firm line along the brow bone. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow pass every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you smooth
steps.voiceScript: Rest your thumbs under the inner ends of your eyebrows, on the bony ridge. Run them outward along the brow bone to the temples, and finish each pass by dropping down in front of the ear. Repeat about ten times.
steps.caution: Work on the bone above the eye socket, never down into the eye.

steps.title: Fan across your forehead
steps.body: Start between your brows and fan your fingertips out to the temples. Work up the forehead line by line until you reach the hairline.
steps.sensationCue: The forehead unclenching. Light, wide, unhurried.
steps.rhythm: One fan every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Long, quiet breaths
steps.voiceScript: Start with your fingertips between your brows. Fan them outward to the temples, lift off, and begin again a little higher up the forehead. Every stroke heads out towards the ears, never side to side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not scrub side to side. Every stroke heads out toward the ears.

steps.title: Empty everything down your neck
steps.body: From behind your ears, stroke down the sides of your neck to the hollows above your collarbones. Twenty slow passes, each lighter than the last.
steps.sensationCue: A downward, emptying feeling. Nothing pressing in.
steps.rhythm: One long stroke every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out along the whole stroke
steps.voiceScript: Everything you have moved forward now needs somewhere to go. Start behind your ears and stroke down the sides of your neck to the hollows above your collarbones, twenty slow times. Make each pass a little lighter than the one before.
steps.caution: Soft sides of the neck only. Never the front of the throat.

steps.title: Rest your palms on your face
steps.body: Cup both palms over your face without pressing. Breathe into your hands three times, then let them fall into your lap.
steps.sensationCue: Warm, still, and lighter around the eyes.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Three slow breaths into your palms
steps.voiceScript: Cup both palms over your face, resting them so gently that nothing presses in. Breathe into your hands three times. Then let your hands fall into your lap and open your eyes slowly.

steps.title: Warm your cheeks and jaw
steps.body: Lay both palms flat over your cheeks. Make slow, wide circles over the whole jaw, letting the skin move with your hands.
steps.sensationCue: Warmth spreading through the cheeks. Nothing sharp.
steps.rhythm: One slow circle every three seconds
steps.breathCue: Slow breath out with each circle
steps.voiceScript: Lay both palms flat over your cheeks, fingers pointing up towards your temples. Make slow, wide circles over the whole jaw and cheek, letting the skin move with your hands rather than sliding across it.

steps.title: Let your jaw hang loose
steps.body: Rest the tip of your tongue behind your top teeth and let your teeth come apart. Sit like that for a slow count of thirty.
steps.sensationCue: The jaw dropping open by itself. No effort at all.
steps.rhythm: Still — just breathing
steps.breathCue: In and out through your nose
steps.voiceScript: Rest the tip of your tongue lightly behind your top teeth and let your back teeth come apart. Lips together, teeth apart. Sit there for a slow count of thirty and notice how much work you were doing without knowing it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not force your mouth open. Just stop holding it shut.

steps.title: Circle the muscle in your cheek
steps.body: Clench once to feel the pad of muscle above your back teeth, then let go. Make slow circles there with two fingertips.
steps.sensationCue: A deep, dull ache that softens as you work. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: About one small circle per second
steps.breathCue: Breathe out and let your jaw go soft
steps.voiceScript: Clench your teeth once and feel the pad of muscle bulge in your cheek, above the back teeth. Now unclench and keep your fingers where that bulge was. Make slow circles there, working both sides at once, and keep the jaw loose while you do it.
steps.commonMistake: Do not work with your teeth clenched. Find the muscle, then let go.

steps.title: Hold the sore spot
steps.body: Find the tenderest point in that muscle and press straight in. Hold still for twenty seconds each side, then ease off slowly.
steps.sensationCue: A strong ache that fades by about half while you hold.
steps.rhythm: Still — hold, do not rub
steps.breathCue: Long breath out into the hold
steps.voiceScript: Search that cheek muscle for the single most tender point, usually about a finger-width in front of your ear lobe. Press straight in with your thumb and hold, without rubbing, for twenty seconds. Ease off slowly, then do the other side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not hunt for more pain. One clear spot per side is plenty.
steps.caution: Gentle pressure only. Stop if you get pain in the ear, the teeth or the joint.

steps.title: Fan out over your temples
steps.body: Put two fingers on each temple. Circle slowly and work outward and upward in a fan, following the muscle above your ear.
steps.sensationCue: A dull tightness easing above the ear. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: One circle every two seconds
steps.breathCue: Quiet, easy breathing
steps.voiceScript: Rest two fingers on each temple. Circle slowly, then fan outward and upward, following that broad chewing muscle in an arc above and behind your ear. Clench once and you will feel exactly where it runs.
steps.commonMistake: Do not press hard on the temple. Light circles do more here.

steps.title: Work inside your cheek
steps.body: With a clean hand, put your thumb inside your cheek and your fingers outside. Gently squeeze the firm band of muscle and hold ten seconds.
steps.sensationCue: A strong but bearable ache in one small band. Never sharp.
steps.rhythm: Hold ten seconds, release, move a little
steps.breathCue: Breathe through your nose and stay loose
steps.voiceScript: Wash your hands first and check your nails are short. Slide your thumb inside your cheek, along the outer edge beside your back teeth, with your fingers on the outside. Squeeze that firm band gently between them, hold for ten seconds, then move a little and repeat.
steps.commonMistake: Do not pinch the soft inner cheek. Aim for the firm band of muscle.
steps.caution: Wash your hands and keep nails short. Stay off the gums, and stop if it hurts.

steps.title: Open and close slowly
steps.body: Rest your tongue on the roof of your mouth and open your mouth slowly, then close it. Keep it small and straight, ten times.
steps.sensationCue: A smooth, even track. No clicking or sliding sideways.
steps.rhythm: One slow open and close every four seconds
steps.breathCue: Breathe out as you open
steps.voiceScript: Rest your tongue on the roof of your mouth and open your jaw slowly, only as far as the tongue stays put. Close just as slowly. Ten small, straight openings, watching that your chin does not drift to one side.
steps.commonMistake: Do not open as wide as you can. Small and smooth is the point.
steps.caution: Stop if your jaw clicks, catches or locks, and get it looked at.

steps.title: Rest your palms and finish
steps.body: Rest both palms over your jaw with no pressure at all. Take three slow breaths, then let your hands fall away.
steps.sensationCue: Warm, still, teeth apart and heavy.
steps.rhythm: Still — no movement
steps.breathCue: Three long breaths out
steps.voiceScript: Rest both palms over your jaw, warm and still, with no pressure at all. Take three slow breaths and let your teeth stay apart. Then let your hands fall into your lap.
steps.commonMistake: Do not go straight back to clenching. Keep your teeth apart.
